title: Fix the Double Free
description: The program should allocate, use, and properly free a block of memory exactly once.
expectedBehavior: The program should allocate, use, and free the memory exactly once, printing 5 without crashing.
actualProblem: free(ptr) is called twice on the same pointer. Freeing already-freed memory is undefined behavior — it can corrupt the heap's internal bookkeeping and crash the program, often unpredictably (sometimes not until much later).
explanation: Each block obtained from malloc()/calloc() should be freed exactly once. Setting the pointer to NULL immediately after freeing it is a common defensive habit, since freeing (or dereferencing) a NULL pointer is safe/detectable, unlike a dangling one.
